page: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in memory-intensive and computational tasks. The instance achieves a Passmark CPU score of 51,024.22 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,097.0, both placing in the strong tier. Single-threaded gzip compression at 33.51 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 223.94 GB/sec also demonstrate strong processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth tests show 2,556.75 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 133.67 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In database operations, the instance handles 58.27 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 14,978.72 on Passmark database tests.

While the r8i.8xlarge excels at memory-bound workloads and smaller-scale AI tasks, achieving a top-tier text generation speed of 404.39 tokens/second on a 135M parameter LLM, it exhibits clear performance tradeoffs on larger models. For instance, text generation speed drops to a weak 2.71 tokens/second when running a 70B parameter LLM, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, DDR5 memory speed, and robust CPU performance, this instance is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise software compilation, and medium-scale data processing workloads.
